display.purpose: The hero line only, centred, with the solid helper set inline as a word.

headline.purpose: Every section title, including the closing question.

title.purpose: Step cards and the job card. Step prices use the same 500 weight and tracking at 1.5rem with tabular figures.

title-sm.purpose: Showcase card titles; the 600 weight is kept for sizes of 1.125rem and below.

question.purpose: FAQ questions, at 500 in the same band as small titles.

wordmark.purpose: The "Seestemic" logotype beside the mark, in the header and the footer; tracked at −0.035em, outside the heading scale.

lead.purpose: The paragraph under each headline, in warm graphite, held to 36rem.

body.purpose: Running text; FAQ answers held to 60ch.

label-sm.purpose: Small buttons, nav links and chips.

small.purpose: The app window's base text, the stage caption and the booking status line; short heads at this size (doc title, phone status bar, footer column heads) step up to 600.

ui.purpose: Text inside depicted product UI, including mini pills at 500, the sidebar preview, the thread subtitle and doc row values; names inside UI step up to 600.

tag.purpose: The Example pill, tool and status pills, and the smallest metadata: timestamps, unread badges, row meta, the phone's day divider and compact tool-tile labels.

numeric.purpose: Tabular Geist figures for times, prices and IDs; there is no mono face.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: White product UI on a painting: the app window, approval panel, job card and phone.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Small white objects: tool tiles on a painting and the white reply bubble on a linen card.

shadows.name: contact
shadows.purpose: Martin's white bubbles in the founder chat: just enough edge to part white from linen without lifting the thread off the card.

shadows.name: hairline-ring
shadows.purpose: The edge of a white object inside UI. Rings, not borders.

shadows.name: ring-soft-drop
shadows.purpose: A white card resting inside UI, such as the doc card. Phone cards and the composer use smaller versions.

shadows.name: window-edge
shadows.purpose: Paired with float on the app window, and with a soft drop on the mobile menu panel.

shadows.name: scrolled-header
shadows.purpose: The header after 8px of scroll, over white at 84% with backdrop-filter: saturate(1.8) blur(18px).

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one ease-out curve for state changes, reveals and entrances.

motion.name: ease-draw
motion.purpose: The line drawing of the closing outline helper: body over 2.2s, eyes over 1s from 1.5s.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Hover and press colour changes on pills, chips and links.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Button press. The composer's send button presses to 0.84.

motion.name: follow
motion.purpose: Helper eyes following the pointer, and demo parts fading up 6px.

motion.name: fade-up
motion.purpose: Panels arriving: the booking panel, the job card on tab switch and the mobile menu at 0.25s. The founder chat's beats use it too, 650ms apart, with movement over 0.6s.

motion.name: blink
motion.purpose: Solid and outline helpers blink. Avatars never do.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every animation and transition collapses. Eyes stay still, and the outline helper is shown complete.

narrative.overview:
Seestemic's page is a quiet white showroom. Near-black Geist, warm gray cards and black pills hold still so that two things can perform: example software floating on impressionist landscapes, and the helper, a speech-bubble character whose eyes follow the visitor around the page. The brief pins the world to xAI's Grok Bot product page. Every asset in it is Seestemic's own: an original mascot, original generated paintings and the Seestemic logo.

Density is low at page level and high inside the product UI. Sections breathe, and type stays compact because the paintings and the giant helpers carry the scale. The helpers break card edges and run off the viewport. Inside the floating windows the system turns dense and exact, with small UI text, 1px hairline rings and spacing tuned pixel by pixel. Motion is soft and decelerating, on one ease-out curve, and most of it belongs to the helper.

Honesty is part of the look. Everything that depicts work is labelled "Example". The page has no logo walls, ratings or metric bands, because there is no approved proof to fill them. The one trust signal is a real person: Martin introduces himself in a short chat, using only facts he has approved. Colour is earned: the interface is ink on white and warm gray, and saturated hue appears only in the paintings, in each helper's own colour and in the tool icons.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, near-black ink, warm gray cards, 1px hairline rules.
One typeface, Geist, at medium weight, with negative tracking that tightens as it grows.
A black pill for the one action and a warm gray pill for the alternative.
Example product UI floating on painted impressionist landscapes.
The helper, a speech-bubble squircle whose eyes follow the pointer. It appears as a word in the headline, as a coloured avatar, and as a giant that breaks its frame.
Flat gray cards. Shadows belong only to white UI lifted off a painting.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Paper Rule
rules.body: The interface itself is achromatic: ink, warm grays and white. Saturation enters only through the paintings, the helper avatars and the tool icons, and status colour stays small and local: blue for new, green for done and brick for a failed load. Buttons, headings and section backgrounds never take a hue.

rules.name: The Blue Is a Signal Rule
rules.body: Brand blue appears only in the logo, the focus ring, the phone's back chevron, text selection and marks of something new: unread counts, the "New" badge and the New Ring. It never fills a button, colours a heading or styles a link. Links are ink with a 1px warm gray underline that darkens on hover.

rules.name: The One Hue per Helper Rule
rules.body: A helper keeps its hue everywhere, and the hue appears only as its avatar body. Any helper larger than an avatar is ink. A tool icon may borrow a helper's hue, always as a glyph on a white tile and never as a body.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Geist is the only typeface. Geist Mono was removed on purpose, so times, prices and IDs use Geist with tabular figures. The world pins Geist, so the detector's "overused font" flag on it is expected and is not a defect.

rules.name: The Medium Voice Rule
rules.body: Display, headline, titles and questions are weight 500. Weight 600 is reserved for the wordmark and for small labels at 1.125rem and below: names in UI, card titles and step numbers. Nothing at heading size is bold.

rules.name: The Tighten-with-Size Rule
rules.body: Tracking is only ever negative, and it grows with size: −0.01em on buttons, −0.012em on small titles and questions, −0.02em on titles, −0.022em on headlines and −0.028em on display. The wordmark is a logotype outside this scale, at −0.035em. Everything is set in sentence case. Headings take no trailing period, though a question keeps its question mark.

rules.name: The One Crop Rule
rules.body: A giant helper is cropped by exactly one edge. The teammate helper rises through its card's top edge and runs off the right of the viewport, and only the card's bottom edge cuts it. The closing outline helper is cut at the waist by the footer's top rule. Never box a giant helper inside its container.

rules.name: The Flat Gray, Floating White Rule
rules.body: Warm gray cards never cast shadows and never carry borders. Shadows belong to white UI, and Float-level shadows appear only where UI sits on a painting.

rules.name: The Speech-Bubble Corner Rule
rules.body: The house silhouette is a rounded rectangle with one tighter corner. The helper's body is a continuous-curvature squircle with three wide corners and a tighter bottom-right tail (48, 48, 20 and 48 units on a 100-unit body). Every chat bubble is an 18–20px rounded rectangle with a single 6px corner pointing at whoever is speaking. When one speaker sends a run of bubbles beside a single photo, as Martin does in the founder chat, only the first bubble takes the corner. The logo echoes the idea: its two large tiles meet at the centre with a square corner.

rules.name: The Nested Corners Rule
rules.body: Radii step down as you go inward: a 32px frame, a 20px window or panel, 16px cards, 12–14px rows, 10px fields and mini rows, 8px attachment chips and focus rings, then pills. A child never has a larger radius than its parent. At 760px and below the outer frames step down a notch: frames to 24px, and the window and tool tiles to 14px. Two shapes keep their own geometry: the composer is 22px, so a one-line reply reads as a pill and a wrapped reply stays a soft rectangle, and the depicted phone is a 54px frame around a 44px screen, concentric across its 10px bezel.

rules.name: The Bleed-Off-the-Bottom Rule
rules.body: Insets inside warm gray cards are open at the bottom. They have rounded top corners (20px for paintings, 18px for mini UI) and square bottom corners, and the card's own edge crops them. Copy sits on top and the inset runs out of the card.

rules.name: The One Black Choice Rule
rules.body: In any set of choices exactly one element is black: the primary action or the current selection. This covers CTA rows, Approve / Edit / Not now, the job tabs and the picked row in a list. Everything else is stone, linen or ghost.

rules.name: The Example Pill Rule
rules.body: Every visual that depicts work carries an "Example" pill. That covers the app window, the approval panel, the memory and handoff lists, and the job stage with its phone. Example content is never presented as a customer, a result or a measurement.

rules.name: The Words on White Rule
rules.body: No running text sits bare on a painting. Every word over art sits on white: the window, a panel, a tile label or the Example pill. Paintings are never scrimmed, tinted or blurred for legibility.

dos: Do keep the page ground white and the interface achromatic: ink text, graphite leads, linen and stone surfaces, and hairline rules.
Do pair one black primary pill with one stone secondary pill in every CTA row (48px tall, 0.75rem apart).
Do float example product UI on a painted landscape inside a 32px frame with the Float shadow, and pin an "Example" pill to it.
Do set headings in Geist 500, tracked tighter as they grow (−0.028em display, −0.022em headline, −0.02em title), in sentence case and without a trailing period.
Do set times, prices and IDs in Geist with tabular figures.
Do let insets bleed off the bottom of warm gray cards, with rounded top corners and square bottom corners cropped by the card.
Do step radii down as you go inward (32, 20, 16, 12, 10px, then pills for controls), and give every chat bubble one 6px corner pointing at its speaker.
Do give each helper its one fixed hue as an avatar, and draw any helper larger than an avatar in ink.
Do let a giant helper break out of its frame, cropped by exactly one edge.
Do honour reduced motion: still eyes, no blinking, and the outline helper shown fully drawn.
donts: Don't add a second typeface. Geist Mono was removed on purpose, and the system has no serif or display face.
Don't use brand blue on buttons, headings, links or large surfaces. It is for the logo, the focus ring, text selection and marks of something new.
Don't put shadows or borders on warm gray cards. Depth belongs to white UI lifted off a painting.
Don't set running text bare on a painting, and don't scrim, tint or blur the art to make it legible. Put the words on white.
Don't set headings bold. Weight 600 is for labels at 1.125rem and below.
Don't put a small label above a section heading. A section opens with its heading and lead.
Don't build testimonial cards, client-logo strips, star ratings or metric bands, and don't ship a demo visual without its Example pill. There is no approved proof to show.
Don't use hard offset shadows, coloured shadows or heavy strokes. Rules and rings are 1px hairlines, small marks inside UI go no heavier than 2px, and the outline helper keeps its own line.
Don't reuse xAI or Grok assets, marks or mascots, and don't swap the paintings for stock photos or flat vector scenes. The world is rebuilt from Seestemic's own helper, logo and generated paintings.
